// CUSTODY LAYER · UNIVERSAL SAFE offline · air-gapped · sovereign

The safe that never talks to the network

Vault is the universal offline safe for Engine-class apps. It stores private keys and login signatures with zero internet permission, seals them inside the phone's secure silicon, signs with your fingerprint, and moves keys to new hardware through light alone — a QR code. Not "we promise not to connect." It cannot connect.

02 / MANDATE WHAT IT GUARDS

One job: be the safe of every sovereign app

Vault is app-agnostic by design. Anything shaped like Engine — an app that wants online life with offline keys — can delegate its identity to the safe.

🗝️
App private keysECDSA P-256 identities generated by apps like Engine, sealed the moment they arrive.
🖋️
Login & wallet signaturesChallenge-response login codes and SPARK wallet transactions — signed inside the safe, never stored online. Every balance change is a signed transaction on an append-only chain.
⟳
Device migration bindingsSigned re-bind records that move your identity to fresh hardware without a cloud backup.
🧿
Fingerprint directoryA local registry of every guarded key, its fingerprint and seal state — visible at a glance.
🚫
Nothing elseNo browsing, no sync, no ads, no telemetry. A safe with a screen, not a smartphone app.
🔓
Biometric-only unlockEvery unseal passes BiometricPrompt with a ±120s freshness window — clock-based replay protection.
03 / CEREMONY HOW AN ONLINE APP SIGNS OFFLINE

The key signs. The key never leaves.

Engine needs a signature → IPC request + challenge → BiometricPrompt → TEE unseals & signs → signed callback → Engine verifies sig + Δt<120s
WHY THE ±120s WINDOW MATTERS The callback signature covers sessionId ‖ status ‖ timestamp. Even a stolen callback cannot be replayed minutes later — the clock is part of the proof. The relay never sees the key; Engine never holds the key; only the TEE ever does.
04 / MIGRATION NEW PHONE, SAME IDENTITY

Moving house through a beam of light

Private keys are the one thing you must never trust to a cloud. When your hardware changes, Vault walks your identity across devices screen-to-screen — step through it below.

🖤
FLAG_SECUREThe QR screen blacks out screenshots and screen recordings. Shoulder-surfing is the only attack left.
Encrypted payloadThe bind URI carries an encrypted session payload — the raw private key never appears in any URI.
Burn after bindingEngine calls convertBoundToPublicKeyOnly() — its private-key copy is wiped the moment Vault takes over.
05 / COMPARISON

Where do keys sleep tonight?

Storage modelNetwork reachExtraction riskMigration path
Browser extension walletalways onlinehigh — memory & disk readableseed phrase on paper
Hot server / custodial24/7 attack surfacesystemic — one breach, all keystrust the operator
Cloud key backupsynced by designaccount compromise = key compromisere-download
Vaultno INTERNET permissionTEE silicon + biometric gateQR light channel, signed re-bind
PHYSICS, NOT PROMISES Every other row in that table depends on someone behaving well. Vault's isolation is declared in the Android manifest and enforced by the OS — a packet cannot be sent, so a promise is never needed.
